methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective, single-center real-world cohort of 363 metastatic NSCLC patients with PD-L1 TPS >= 50% and no actionable drivers treated with first-line pembrolizumab, with systematic thyroid testing at baseline and every six weeks. The design is appropriate for evaluating incidence/timing of irTD and its association with PFS, and key exclusions (pre-existing thyroid dysfunction) and outcome definitions are described. A major strength is the explicit effort to address immortal-time bias by modeling irTD as a time-varying covariate and performing 3- and 6-month landmark analyses. Limitations include the single-center retrospective nature, incomplete baseline covariates (e.g., broader genomic profiling, autoimmune history, steroids), and potential surveillance-intensity confounding.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual cohort study (real-world retrospective) evaluating an on-treatment biomarker association with outcomes, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical relevance is high because irTD is common (110/363; 30.3%), is low-grade/manageable, and is strongly associated with longer PFS, potentially informing patient counseling and monitoring expectations. The study does not establish causality, and irTD is an on-treatment event rather than a baseline selection tool, so it is not yet a decision rule. Nonetheless, the association is clinically meaningful and aligns with the need for practical biomarkers in PD-L1-high NSCLC treated with pembrolizumab.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for this retrospective observational cohort, and the manuscript reports eligibility criteria (PD-L1 threshold, driver exclusion, timeframe), outcome definitions, irTD definitions, CTCAE grading, and key baseline characteristics. The statistical approach is described and includes time-varying Cox modeling and landmark analyses to mitigate immortal-time bias, with effect estimates and confidence intervals reported for PFS. Limitations are explicitly stated, including restricted molecular testing and missing baseline variables. Data/code sharing is not described in the blinded manuscript, so reproducibility support is limited.

novelty_literature.justification: The association between immune-related adverse events, including thyroid dysfunction, and improved outcomes on immune checkpoint inhibitors has been studied, so the core hypothesis is not entirely new. The manuscript's contribution is a relatively large, homogeneous first-line pembrolizumab PD-L1-high NSCLC cohort with systematic thyroid monitoring and explicit bias-mitigation via time-dependent and landmark analyses. It also evaluates timing (early vs. late irTD) and finds no differential PFS by timing, which is a useful nuance. Overall, novelty is moderate: a solid extension and strengthening rather than a first-in-class finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitatively specific, reporting irTD incidence, onset timing, and large PFS differences with hazard ratios and landmark confirmations. Methods are organized with clear definitions (irTD, early vs. late, testing schedule) and standard response/toxicity frameworks (RECIST and CTCAE). Results are presented with cohort descriptors and the main comparative effect estimates, and the discussion connects findings to bias concerns and prior studies. Overall clarity and structure are strong for a retrospective real-world analysis.

key_strengths: Large single-center first-line pembrolizumab cohort restricted to PD-L1 TPS >= 50% and no actionable drivers with systematic thyroid monitoring
Strong analytic handling of immortal-time bias using time-varying covariates and 3- and 6-month landmark analyses
Clinically interpretable findings: irTD incidence 30.3%, all grade 1-2 with no discontinuations, and a strong association with improved PFS
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with potential residual confounding related to treatment duration, surveillance, and unmeasured baseline factors
Limited molecular profiling (EGFR/ALK only) may leave residual oncogene-addicted cases and affects generalizability
On-treatment biomarker association risks reverse causation (patients doing well stay on therapy longer and have more opportunity to develop irTD) despite bias-mitigation steps
Data/code availability not described, limiting reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is methodologically stronger than many irAE-outcome associations because it explicitly addresses immortal-time bias and uses a large homogeneous cohort, supporting a clinically meaningful signal. However, because it remains retrospective and single-center with unmeasured confounding and limited molecular profiling, it would likely require major revisions and cautious claims for acceptance at a tier-2 journal.
